body.estimand_functional: \(I_n^{\mathrm{SI}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\theta\in\Theta:\text{the bias-aware transformed-outcome test at the scan-selected cutoff accepts }\theta\}\)

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and a law-specific unknown cutoff \(c_P\in[1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument is \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge c_P\}\), and monotone response types imply \(D_i=D_i(Z_i)\).
sampling_model.outcome: Binary potential outcomes obey consistency \(Y_i=Y_i(D_i)\); exclusion is encoded by the absence of a direct \(Z_i\) argument.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniformly on both sides of the cutoff, \(\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x,\ell)\ge v\) and the absolute conditional outcome--treatment correlation is at most \(1-v\); when the conditional treatment variance is zero, covariance is zero and the correlation inequality is interpreted directly without forming a correlation coefficient.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: One-sided observable treatment and outcome regressions admit radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions; local-polynomial regression and cutoff classification use deterministic sample folds.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 states that the bias-aware Anderson--Rubin confidence set is honest over the maintained known-cutoff class.
Their Theorem 4 establishes \(n\)-consistent cutoff estimation with a compound-Poisson argmax limit under a fixed discontinuity.
Their ordered-modulus construction minimizes expected length at a point subject to uniform coverage over a convex regression class.
Their Proposition 4.2 gives a matched minimax cutoff-location rate when the derivative jump is bounded away from zero.
Their multiscale estimator provides simultaneous change-point inference and exponential underestimation control for step functions.
Their Bayesian model propagates posterior uncertainty about an unknown cutoff into fuzzy-RD effect estimation.
Their working paper treats fuzzy regression discontinuity and unknown discontinuity estimation in separate high-dimensional extensions.

body.tldr: The paper determines the minimax fixed-\(\alpha\) expected length of connected honest confidence intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE when the compliance jump \(\kappa_n\) and its unknown cutoff vanish in statistical visibility together. A causal location-mixture subexperiment yields a nonshrinking lower bound below \(T_n=n\kappa_n^{2+1/s}\asymp\log(1/\kappa_n)\), even when the known-cutoff interval shrinks and even when outcomes are observed. A scan--refine--invert interval recovers the known-cutoff order above this boundary. The central open theorem evaluates and matches the fixed-level length in the critical window by combining sharp compensation profiles, truncated location mixtures, and effect-label testing.

project_justification.gap: Weak fuzzy-RD inference is honest at a known cutoff, and unknown-cutoff theory localizes directly observed fixed or shrinking jumps, but neither literature characterizes connected LATE-interval length when the first-stage denominator and its location become weak jointly.
project_justification.niche: The joint experiment has a nonconvex location union, a causal outcome--treatment coupling, and a fixed-level decision loss; its critical window cannot be read from a point-estimation cutoff rate or a known-cutoff weak-instrument inversion.
project_justification.fill: The project defines the minimax problem by observable one-sided reduced forms, an outcome-variance floor, a treatment--outcome correlation separation, and a factor-two first-stage shell that indexes uniform risk at strength \(\kappa_n\); it embeds an outcome-invariant latent monotone packing in that class, derives a finite-sample connected-length converse, constructs a four-fold bias-aware scan--invert interval, and evaluates the remaining critical-window experiment with an explicit attainment result.

body.related_work: Noack and Rothe (2024) motivate the observable class: fuzzy-RD LATE is a ratio of one-sided reduced-form jumps, weak compliance defeats ordinary Wald inference, and bias-aware Anderson--Rubin inversion restores known-cutoff honesty under smooth observed regressions. Porter and Yu (2015) organize unknown-cutoff RD into detection, cutoff estimation, and effect estimation, but their oracle substitution argument relies on a fixed discontinuity and centers on sharp RD. M{\"u}ller and Song (1997) derive a triangular-drift Brownian localization limit for a vanishing regression jump, while Tuvaandorj (2020) obtains white-noise equivalence and minimax location rates under a jump floor; these results inform the local cutoff coordinate rather than the causal interval-length claim. Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018) supply the ordered-modulus and test-inversion template for fixed-level expected length on convex regression classes. Frick, Munk, and Sieling (2014) supply the multiscale scan architecture for step signals, and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014) supply Gaussian coupling and anti-concentration for the cutoff--scale maximum. Madrid Padilla, Yu, Wang, and Rinaldo (2022) show how aligned multivariate change channels affect localization, but their signal vectors are unrestricted rather than constrained by a monotone fuzzy-RD causal model. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version) jointly model fuzzy effects and an unknown cutoff in a Bayesian specification without a frequentist honest minimax frontier. Arai, Otsu, and Seo (2026) treat fuzzy and unknown-discontinuity extensions separately, leaving the joint weak-cutoff object untouched.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The displayed quartic family certifies the logarithmic barrier but is not asserted to solve the normalized compensation problem. The untruncated second-moment expression loses sharpness when \(n\kappa_n^{2+1/s}\) is comparable to \(\log(1/\kappa_n)\); boundary truncation, mixture renormalization, and effect-label testing must be retained in the critical-window proof.
body.honest_scope: The Wald interpretation, finite-sample location barrier, known-cutoff order, and strong-signal scan--invert claim are supporting results to be proved uniformly over the observable reduced-form class. The factor-two shell \(\kappa_n\le d_P\le2\kappa_n\) is this proposal's strength-indexed triangular slice defining uniform minimax risk at scale \(\kappa_n\), not an assumption attributed to Noack and Rothe (2024). The class uses their observable outcome-variance and correlation-separation form, including the zero-treatment-variance convention, and does not impose a covariance-matrix eigenvalue floor. The exact fixed-\(\alpha\) critical-window value and its attaining connected interval stand as Open-ended Question 1. Its small-\(\lambda\) requirement is only to recover Theorem 2's converse unless a separate attaining upper bound is established. At a supplied cutoff the proposal reduces to the known-cutoff weak-fuzzy-RD order, and in the fixed-jump face the scan--refine step reduces to the oracle unknown-cutoff logic of Porter and Yu (2015). Latent-cell H\"older smoothness and four-cell positivity are properties of the explicit witness, not restrictions on the minimax class. No claim is made about disconnected confidence-set optimality, adaptation to unknown \(s\), or Bayesian credible-set calibration.
